creationPrompt:
Create a developer onboarding for me as a Claw Me Page. Include a useful repository map, first contribution, when setup fails. Ask only for missing information in one concise batch: repository, supported runtimes, verified setup commands, architecture map, access needs, tests and contribution workflow.

Use semantic responsive HTML, working section links, and useful native details/summary interactions. No scripts, forms, tracking, or embedded frames in the static Page. PDF export is separate from Page publishing unless the current platform explicitly supports it.

exampleAnswers.Purpose and audience: A developer onboarding guide with repository orientation, setup checks, and a first contribution.
exampleAnswers.Working context: This fictional guide introduces a static handover-template repository. Commands describe the example workflow and should be replaced with the actual project’s verified setup instructions.
exampleAnswers.Example records:
Step: Read the working agreement · Purpose: Understand scope and workflow · Completion check: Branch and review rules are clear
Step: Inspect a template · Purpose: Learn the source structure · Completion check: HTML, metadata, and brief located
Step: Build locally · Purpose: Produce a portable artifact · Completion check: Example page opens correctly
Step: Make a small change · Purpose: Practice the contribution path · Completion check: Diff is focused and checked
Step: Request review · Purpose: Share evidence and limits · Completion check: Reviewer can reproduce the result
exampleAnswers.Content decisions:
A useful repository map: Start with the README, contributor agreement, template catalog, shared styles, and build script. Identify which files are canonical and which are generated before editing either.
First contribution: Improve one unclear label or a small content example. Build the artifact, check desktop and mobile output, and explain the user-visible change in the review description.
When setup fails: Record the command, expected result, actual error, and relevant runtime version. Keep secrets out of logs and ask the responsible maintainer about missing access rather than inventing configuration values.
exampleAnswers.Format and interaction: manual layout; section navigation and expandable detail where useful; matching portrait document PDF.
exampleAnswers.Sharing and provenance: A hypothetical example informed by Claw Me’s small-team and Agent workflows. These are not Pete’s actual clients, finances, travel plans, research results, or commitments. Keep the real adaptation private until the owner chooses to share.
